thread.title: Will the bearish Dow streak infect the rest of the stock market? - MarketWatch

author: Simon Maierhofer
title: Will the bearish Dow streak infect the rest of the stock market? - MarketWatch
text:
The Russell 2000 Index of small-cap stocks has been racing from one all-time high to the next, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 Index are slacking.
In fact, the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -0.66% is 7% below its high and just suffered seven consecutive down days.
This kind of divergence has been likened to soldiers (small-cap stocks) running up the hill, while the generals (large-cap stocks) are waiting to commit.
Read: Robust U.S. economy isn’t speeding up, but isn’t slowing down either
The implication is clear: The generals know something the soldiers don’t.
The chart below highlights the fragmented nature of the stock market:
• iShares Russell 2000 ETF IWM, -0.59% set a new all-time high on June 20.
• Nasdaq-100 ETF QQQ, -0.52% set a new intraday all-time high on June 20.
• Dow Jones SPDR ETF DIA, -0.67% is 7% below its Jan. 26 all-time high.
• S&P 500 SPDR ETF SPY, -0.49% is still 3.7% below its Jan. 26 all-time high.
Despite the large divergence between Russell 2000 RUT, -0.60% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average, statistics do not support the bearish generals/soldiers theory.
The last two times we saw a similar divergence was in September 1997 (in the middle of one of the greatest bull markets) and February 2000 (at the end of one of the greatest bull markets). There’s no edge here.
Divergence explained A rising tide lifts all boats, but every boat is different.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is price-weighted. Boeing BA, -1.10% UnitedHealth UNH, -0.55% Goldman Sachs GS, -0.35% and 3M MMM, -1.04% account for almost a third of the Dow.
The Nasdaq COMP, -0.53% and S&P 500 SPX, -0.48% are bullied by tech juggernauts like Apple AAPL, -0.25% and Amazon AMZN, -0.78%
GrubHub GRUB, -2.14% and nearly 2,000 even smaller companies make up the Russell 2000.
Every index is different, and should be analyzed based on its own individual merit.
The chart above shows individual support/resistance and breakout levels for IWM, QQQ, SPY and DIA.
The May 23 Profit Radar Report said: “The Russell 2000 IWM ETF remains above support (green line) with strong RSI [relative strength index] and on balance volume. Unless reversed by a drop below support, IWM looks bullish. The Nasdaq-100 QQQ ETF reversed from a 5-day low to a 5-day high. That’s happened six other times. Two weeks later QQQ was up 85% of the time.”
The IWM and QQQ charts remain bullish. While SPY and DIA are still stuck in large trading ranges — based on liquidity and Elliott Wave theory — there’s a 70% chance they will grind higher before suffering the next bigger pullback.
A detailed longer-term analysis for the S&P 500 is available here: S&P 500 outlook .
